fatal_errors: The proposed polycrystalline copper is unrelated to the target equiatomic FCC Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-derived single crystals.
The tensile-test geometry, 300–800 K range, and 10^-3 s^-1 strain rate do not reconstruct the target compression experiments conducted from 9 to 1373 K at 10^-4 s^-1.
The hypothesis omits the defining cryogenic inertial dulling, MSAD-dependent solid-solution strengthening, and high-temperature Portevin–Le Chatelier behavior.
The numerical strength predictions are uncited and internally inconsistent: a 15 MPa decrease per 100 K over 300–800 K implies a 75 MPa change, not the stated 40 MPa change.
The proposed measurements cannot distinguish dislocation glide, climb, and grain-boundary sliding or test the target Cottrell-versus-Suzuki mechanisms.
explanation: The response addresses temperature-dependent deformation only at a generic level. Thermally activated dislocation motion and lower strength at higher temperature are qualitatively plausible for copper, but almost none of the target material, specimen state, conditions, composition-dependent mediators, characteristic low- and high-temperature regimes, or discriminating measurements are recovered. No supporting evidence is supplied, and the quantitative predictions and falsification criterion are not physically or arithmetically well disciplined.
